cell_edits.Est. cost & time: RSD 6,500 APR registration fee + translations/apostille; ~1-2 months (statutory 30 days)

finding: APR states the fee for registering the formation of an association is RSD 6,500, which contradicts the '~2,000-5,000 RSD fees' in the cost cell. The Ministry guide to the Law on Associations confirms 3+ founders with at least one resident or seated in Serbia, a representative with residence or temporary stay in Serbia, and a 30-day APR registration term.

Montenegro's Law on NGOs (SL CG 39/11, 37/17) Art. 10 requires at least three founders for an association, one of whom must have residence, stay or seat in Montenegro, while a foundation may be founded by one or more persons regardless of residence. The register is kept by the Ministry of Public Administration and registration is free; online registration was not available as of the latest civil-society reports.

Philea's 2025 profile confirms that North Macedonian foundations need an initial asset pool of at least EUR 10,000 and register with the Central Register, filing within 30 days of the founding act. Associations require five founders under the Law on Associations and Foundations, and registration takes about 5 days once the file is complete; the exact official fee is not published in these sources.

cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Albanian-language documents + local office; filing with the Tirana court NPO register (post/courier accepted), limited English support.

finding: Under Law 80/2021, as partly struck down by Constitutional Court Decision No. 62 of 20 Nov 2023, NPO registration decisions are made by a judge of the Tirana judicial district court and the court is the sole competent registration body. The bottleneck cell's reference to 'QKB electronic filing' (the National Business Center) is therefore inaccurate; the official court fee schedule was not found.

Moldova's Law 86/2020 on Non-commercial Organisations governs associations, foundations and private institutions, and registration with the Public Services Agency is free. The term was cut from 30 to 15 days, and individuals may found associations regardless of citizenship or residence.

The existing Ukraine cells are consistent with Law 4572-VI on Public Associations and Law 5073-VI on Charitable Activities. That law lets foreigners found an association only if they are lawfully staying in Ukraine, and state registration of a public association is free. No source found contradicts the current values.

cell_edits.Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1+ founder with initial assets of at least 100x the gross minimum wage (OG 26/2000 Art. 15), notary deed.

finding: Article 15 of OG 26/2000 requires a Romanian foundation's initial assets to be worth at least 100 times the gross minimum wage at the date of incorporation (20 times for pure fund-raising foundations), so 'endowment per charter' was wrong. The exact court/state registration fee could not be confirmed from an official schedule.

Initial registration of a Bulgarian NPLE in the Registry Agency costs BGN 50 (EUR 25.56) on paper or half that if filed electronically. Associations need 3 founders (7 natural or 3 legal persons for public benefit), and foreign founders face no residence requirement and can act via an apostilled notarised power of attorney. The registrar decides within 3 business days of filing.

cell_edits.Main charitable entity types: Associations (somateio, min. 20 founders, Civil Code art. 78); foundations (Civil Code arts. 108-121 + Law 4182/2013, to be largely repealed by Law 5259/2025 once its Unit I takes effect); general-benefit status via separate application.

finding: Article 131 of Greece's Law 5259/2025 repeals arts. 1-76 and 80-82 of Law 4182/2013 only from the entry into force of Unit I. Unit I in turn waits on two declaratory acts (arts. 5(5) and 7(3)), which the government MITOS portal still listed as pending on 2 Sep 2026. Philea confirms that associations need 20 founders and are registered by the Magistrate's Court.

cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Trust unregistered (easiest); registered society needs Cypriot head office + 20 founding members + local agent for bank account

finding: Under Cyprus's Societies and Institutions Law 104(I)/2017, a society is an association of at least 20 persons registered by the District Officer acting as Registrar/Commissioner. That contradicts the bottleneck cell's '7 members'. An institution needs no members but must have dedicated property of at least EUR 1,000; the society registration fee amount was not found in official sources.

In Malta, the Foundations and Associations Unit of the Malta Business Registry registers legal organisations under the Second Schedule of the Civil Code. Enrolment as a voluntary organisation with the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations costs a one-time EUR 40 and requires at least three administrators. These match the existing cells, though the exact MBR registration fee schedule could not be retrieved.

The CRO fee leaflet lists EUR 100 to incorporate a new company on a paper Form A1 or EUR 50 online via CORE, consistent with the ~EUR 100 / ~$110 figures. Registration with the Charities Regulator is free. Nothing found contradicts the s.137 EEA-resident director or bond requirement.
